g.text: The work depends on two things: which resource it is, and which operation you are running.
Without Visitor: a type check in every operation
if (r instanceof Server) { ... }
else if (r instanceof Database) { ... }
else if (r instanceof LoadBalancer) { ... }
The same chain again in the security audit.
And again in the tagging report.
With Visitor: two hops, no type check
1. resource.accept(visitor)
the caller does not know the type
2. visitor.visit(this)
the resource does, so it selects the method
Two hops. That is called double dispatch.
Adding an operation is cheap
MonthlyCost, SecurityAudit, a tagging report, a diagram
export: each one is a new class, and no resource
class changes.
Adding a resource type is expensive
A new Queue type means a new visit method on the
interface, and every visitor written so far has to
implement it.
So Visitor fits one situation: the set of types is stable, and the set of operations keeps growing.
If your types change more often than your operations, the pattern is the wrong way round and will cost more than it saves.
